answer.rationale: Finance mandate of 18% spend cut is non-negotiable and incumbent has refused reopening. Memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlocked volume pricing, but that leverage is exhausted. Memory_c4 shows renegotiation can work, but only when the incumbent has reputational incentive—they've already refused. Memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to a low-cost vendor delivered sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. At 94% volume utilization with 14-day deadline, we have limited negotiating runway. A standard experiment with the low-cost vendor addresses the 18% mandate while memory_c1 and memory_c3 together mitigate the single point of failure risk (add second source in next cycle). However, this elevates delivery risk in the short term given the tight assembly line buffer. Verification of memory_c2 confirms the low-cost vendor's historical execution reliability before commitment.
